text:
Ilya Sorokin remains what he has been for years: the reason the Islanders stay in games they have no business staying in. Through 11 starts he has saved 6.05 goals above expected (saves beyond what the quality of shots predicts) and he stops 86% of high-danger shots, 84th percentile in the league. Last season he finished 22.3 above expected over 55 games, which is star territory.

The last stretch has been leaner. His last five starts netted 2.41 below expected, and the latest loss to New Jersey was a shooting gallery: NHL.com's Stefen Rosner kept posting about right-pad robberies on Nico Hischier before a puck banked in off him. That is the kind of week where the goalie is fine and the team in front of him is the story.

One oddity: he ranks only 33rd of 75 in our wins added, likely because his best saves came when they moved the result less. We trust the shot-quality numbers more here. Our talent estimate keeps him above league average, and we'd expect the five-game dip to look like noise by December.
headline: Sorokin is still elite, even through a cold week
